pages.text: Whaley is a blue whale, the biggest animal on Earth. He lives in the wide ocean and swims slowly, calmly, and gently.
The ocean is huge. Some places are shallow and sunny, and some places are very deep, cold, and dark.
Ocean water is salty. It tastes salty, not sweet. Salt is mixed into the water everywhere in the sea.
Whaley swishes his strong tail up and down. That tail push helps him move forward through heavy water.
Even though Whaley lives in water, he must breathe air. He cannot breathe underwater like fish can.
Whaley swims up to the surface. He blows air out through his blowhole, making a tall spray called a spout.
Whaley eats tiny food called krill. He opens his mouth wide, then filters the water and keeps the krill.
Some ocean parts are so deep that sunlight cannot reach. Down there, it can feel very dark and quiet.
Whaley listens to sounds in the water. Whales can make calls, and sound can travel far in the ocean.
Whaley keeps swimming, breathing air, and eating krill. The ocean is his home, and he helps it stay healthy.
At bedtime, we remember: the biggest whale lives in salty water, and deep ocean can be cold, dark, and calm.
